text:
Jen Harris: Quick sync: Auth team wants to start enforcing `aud` claim on JWTs for API v2. Some older clients (embedded devices, legacy SDKs) omit aud. We need a compatibility strategy before enforcement.
Omar Faruk: How many callers are we talking about? Any high-volume flows?
Jen Harris: Small set: ~6 internal integrations, 9 partners, some device fleet telem pings. Estimated auths without aud ~2-3k/day. Not huge but customer-impacting.
Sasha Li: Options: 1) Deploy an auth shim that accepts tokens without aud but performs stricter origin verification + short TTL; 2) Soft-fail (allow but log and emit metric) then flip to hard reject after grace; 3) Exchange endpoint: clients POST old token, get v2 token with aud.
Omar Faruk: I prefer the exchange endpoint. Keeps core services checking `aud`, avoids changing many services. But need to limit blast radius: rate-limit exchanges per-tenant, require client proof-of-possession maybe, and mark tokens issued via exchange with `x-compat=true`.
Jen Harris: Security constraints: exchange should validate signature, check issuer, and only issue a scoped v2 token with minimal scopes and short expiry (15m). Audit every exchange. No anonymous exchanges. Use Vault-stored signing keys.
Sasha Li: Alternative shim at edge could add an `aud` claim on the fly and pass through, but that bypasses service-level verification auditability. Not ideal long-term.
Omar Faruk: Rollout plan: announce deprecation + enforcement window (60 days). Start by shipping a soft-monitor mode in Auth that logs `jwt.missing_aud` and increments `jwt.missing_aud.count`. After 2 weeks of monitoring, enable the exchange endpoint + feature-flag per-tenant `compat_aud_exchange`. Canary exchange at 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% over one week.
Jen Harris: Add an escape hatch header `X-RW-Allow-Legacy-AUD: true` that the bridge honors only when tenant flag is enabled and when request originates from allowed IPs / origins. Must be replay-protected.
Sasha Li: nginx+lua exchange-forward snippet for edge: ```lua local legacy = ngx.req.get_headers()["x-old-jwt"]; if legacy then local res = ngx.location.capture("/auth-exchange", { method = ngx.HTTP_POST, body = legacy }); if res.status == 200 then ngx.req.set_header("Authorization", "Bearer " .. res.body); else ngx.exit(res.status); end end ```
Omar Faruk: Metrics & alerts: emit `jwt.missing_aud.count`, `aud_exchange.requests`, `aud_exchange.success`, `aud_exchange.failure`. Alert if `aud_exchange.failure / aud_exchange.requests > 0.02` for 5m. Also track `jwt.missing_aud.unhandled` to see who would break.
Jen Harris: Tests: unit tests for exchange proto, integration test with a token missing aud should succeed via exchange and fail otherwise. Add property test for replay protection.
Sasha Li: Developer DX: SDK helper `rw_auth.ensureAud()` that detects missing aud and calls exchange; include sample code for iOS/Android. Publish migration guide and a sandbox endpoint partners can use.
Omar Faruk: Legal ops: confirm we can permit exchange-based tokens under current contracts for 60-day window. Loop in Legal.
Jen Harris: Ops: runbook for when exchange floods: kill-switch `compat_aud_exchange` false; block by tenant; throttle at edge. Ensure Console shows `jwt.missing_aud` events for tenant debugging.
deploy-bot: starting canary deploy for `auth-exchange` in edge-eu at 4132154500.
ops-bot: canary traffic routing -> 0.5% -> monitoring hooks attached.
Sasha Li: Action owners: Sasha implement exchange + proto, Omar add metrics/alerts + runbook, Jen own tenant comms + deprecation notice, ops add dashboard tiles for `jwt.missing_aud`.
Jen Harris: Timeline: announce today, monitoring window 14 days, enable exchange canary after monitoring, widen over 7 days, enforce `aud` at 60 days.
Omar Faruk: One more thing: mark tokens minted by exchange with claim `compat: "aud-exchange"` so downstream analytics can filter.
Jen Harris: Good call. We'll reconvene after canary telemetry. :white_check_mark:
